meta.not_covered_reason: These are argued from the literature, from figures, or from experiments not yet run; they carry no figure this script could compute.

UNITS.title: Analysis units
UNITS.asks: (structural) R1 objected to pseudo-replication in the earlier 33/33. Four distinct units are separated here, and every rate names the one it uses.

audit_sessions.definition: one audit_*.jsonl file, i.e. one navigator start
audit_sessions.note: Sessions carrying no decision record are kept as provenance and are never counted as observations.

runs.definition: an audit session containing at least one decision cycle
runs.note: A recovery cycle inside a run that later reaches its destination is not a failed mission. Outcome is taken from the last record of the run.

decision_cycles.definition: one decision record; a run may contain several
decision_cycles.used_for: VLM calls, guard activations, resolution path
decision_cycles.composition: 226 decision cycles = 212 records that reached a resolution or were blocked by a guard, plus 14 records whose L3b call returned no parseable JSON.

semantic_units.definition: one instruction intent / sealed cell / stored association
semantic_units.note: Repetitions of one intent are observations within a cluster. They are evidence of repeatability, not independent semantic cases.

BLOCKS.title: Experimental blocks of session E
BLOCKS.asks: (structural) what each block tested and which point it answers.

E0.title: Start gate
E0.tests: Warm-up and verification that the configured digest, graph and ontology match the sealed values before any measured run.

E1.title: Post-arrival visual confirmation after the ontology correction
E1.tests: Re-test of arrival confirmation once fire_hydrant_cb202 was corrected to fire_extinguisher_cb202, including the arm in which the extinguisher was physically removed.
E1.component: L3 post-arrival confirmation; static semantic ontology
E1.prior_sessions: Confirmation was reported but never re-tested against a corrected ontology, and no arm varied the physical referent.

E2.rate_note: A low fast-path rate is the intended outcome. A negated instruction should not be resolved deterministically; escalation or a block is the correct behaviour.
E2.title: Negation, location conflict, controls
E2.tests: Negated instructions, instructions whose location referent conflicts with the semantic referent, and matched controls.
E2.prior_sessions: The mechanism did not exist. No record in sessions A-C can show negation handling of any kind.

E3.title: Verification re-run on the declared experimental unit
E3.tests: Repetition of resolved instructions with the unit of analysis declared in advance, so repeated measures can be grouped.
E3.prior_sessions: Repetitions exist but no unit of analysis was declared, so they were counted as independent observations.

E4.rate_note: Fast path is 0% by construction: the block issues L3b calls in order to accumulate association candidates.
E4.title: Promotion stability: rejection of unstable associations
E4.tests: Whether repeated L3b resolutions of the same instruction converge closely enough to be promoted into deterministic memory. Both candidates fell below the consistency threshold and neither was promoted, so this block does not demonstrate transfer; E4b does.
E4.prior_sessions: Session B ran on the digest compiled from session A, but the induction and the transfer were not run as one controlled sequence.

E4b.rate_note: The fast-path records are the point of the block: they are the transferred preference being served at cascade step 0 on the second platform.
E4b.title: Second induction, end to end
E4b.tests: The same transfer repeated as a single uninterrupted chain, with the digest recompiled and reinstalled between platforms.

E5.rate_note: Fast path is 0% by construction; the block issues VLM calls deliberately to load the shared server.
E5.title: Concurrency on the shared VLM server
E5.tests: Both platforms issuing VLM requests against one server, with destinations chosen so the routes cannot intersect.
E5.prior_sessions: Session C ran both platforms concurrently, but with four decisions and no latency comparison against single-platform operation.

E6.rate_note: Fast path is 0% by construction: the digest is removed, so no M3 preference can match.
E6.title: Full semantic-memory ablation
E6.tests: The same instructions with the compiled digest removed. That takes away M3 step-0 matching AND the M1/M2 prefix of the L3b prompt, so it ablates the whole memory layer, not M3 in isolation.
E6.component: compiled memory digest (M3 matching + M1/M2 prompt prefix)

primary_unit.label: sealed instruction cell
primary_unit.note: 29 decision cycles represent 28 sealed cells; one cell was executed twice

E7.rate_note: The only block whose fast-path rate estimates performance on instructions the system had not seen.
E7.title: Sealed instruction set
E7.tests: Instructions written from a university-corridor repertoire and sealed, with their acceptance criteria, before the system saw them.
E7.component: Full L3 pipeline on unseen instructions
E7.prior_sessions: Never performed. Every instruction in sessions A-C was constructed around the scenarios being demonstrated.

fast_path_primary.note: 29 decision cycles represent 28 sealed cells; one cell was executed twice

metrics.composition_note: The session-wide fast-path rate is an artefact of how many records each block contributed, not a property of the system. Blocks E1 and E3 issued no VLM call at all, while E7 escalated most of its instructions. Rates must be read per block; the aggregate is reported only alongside this composition.

R1-1.title: Scope of validation and inclusion criterion
R1-1.asks: Delimit the novelty claim and state which decisions are counted.

metrics.convention_note: An "escalated" record is an L3b attempt that returned no parseable JSON. It is an attempt, not a completed decision. Both counts are reported; they must not be mixed. The delivery manifest quotes the second figure.

R1-2.title: Experimental unit for transfer
R1-2.asks: 33 transfers are not 33 independent cases; identify the experimental unit.

E4_promotion_stability.role: accumulation of association candidates. Not a transfer experiment: neither candidate met the promotion criterion, so nothing was promoted and nothing could transfer.

metrics.canonical_claim: One independently induced instruction-node association was promoted on one platform and subsequently reused deterministically on the other in 4/4 recipient trials, at cascade step 0 with no VLM call. The repetitions evidence reliability of that one reuse; they are not independent transfers.
metrics.do_not_report: a pooled count of E4 and E4b decision records as "transfer records". They are promotion-related decision records, and most of them belong to a block that produced no transfer.

R1-3.title: Operator preferences vs learned associations
R1-3.asks: Preferences were learned from repetition, not declared by an operator.

m3_reuse_hits.definition: decision records whose audit field m3_promotion_triggered is true. The field marks REUSE of an already-stored preference, not the creation of one: every such record resolves by L3a_m3_preference at cascade step 0 against a stored entry.

metrics.note: No record carries an operator confirmation field, because the system has no such mechanism. The absence is a declared limitation, measurable here as: zero of 226 records were operator-confirmed.

R1-4.title: Fast-path rate and the distribution it was measured on
R1-4.asks: 88% reflects a constructed instruction distribution, not natural traffic.

e7_sealed_set.unit: sealed cell (28); the block holds 29 records because one cell ran twice
e7_sealed_set.description: Instructions written and sealed before any run, from a university-corridor repertoire, with acceptance criteria fixed in the same sealed file.

false_fast_resolution.definition: a cell the resolver answered deterministically, with no VLM call, and got wrong. The most consequential failure mode: confident, fast, and incorrect.

R1-5.title: Ablation of the compiled memory digest (full memory layer)
R1-5.asks: Baselines and ablations separating the contribution of each component.

metrics.what_is_removed: M3 step-0 preference matching and the M1/M2 memory prefix in the L3b prompt. This is an ablation of the whole compiled memory layer, not of M3 in isolation.
metrics.attribution_limit: The shift from L3a to L3b is attributable to the absence of M3. The change of selected node is not attributable to M3 alone, because the L3b prompt also lost its M1/M2 context. Isolating M1/M2 from M3 would need a further ablation that was not run.

R1-7.title: Repeated measures, effect sizes, and an external localization reference
R1-7.asks: Identify the experimental unit; grouped or hierarchical analysis; confidence intervals for latency ratios and effect sizes; an external localization reference to establish the causality of AMCL drift.

metrics.decision_latency_ratio_escalated_over_fa: see the LATENCY key: three distinct estimands are reported there, and the between-arm ratio is computed once, with E0 excluded. It is not recomputed here, so the report cannot carry two values for it.
metrics.separation_note: Cliff's delta of exactly -1 means complete separation: every fast-path decision is faster than every escalated one. The effect size is reported for completeness, but with no overlap the informative statistic is the ratio and its interval.
metrics.note: Intervals are produced by resampling clusters, not observations. Resampling observations would treat repetitions of one instruction as independent, which is the objection being answered.

LATENCY.title: Latency: three distinct estimands
LATENCY.asks: (structural) keep the three latency ratios apart.

between_arm_unpaired.question: across the session, how far apart are decisions taken on the deterministic path and decisions that escalated?
between_arm_unpaired.design: unpaired; different instructions on the two arms

within_instruction_paired.question: for the same instruction on the same platform, what does removing the compiled memory cost?
within_instruction_paired.design: paired within instruction and platform (E6 vs its memory-on twin)
within_instruction_paired.interval: reported as a range over the paired units, n is small

result.estimand: within-instruction, within-platform ratio of decision latency with memory removed over memory present

within_case_transfer.question: for the one association actually promoted, what did the recipient robot gain?
within_case_transfer.design: within case, same platform, same instruction, before and after promotion (E4b phase 0 vs phase 3)
within_case_transfer.interval: none. The baseline is a single VLM call. This is a mechanistic illustration of the transfer, not an estimate with sampling precision, and must be labelled as such.

metrics.warning: These three answer different questions. Presenting the first as the "statistical version" of the third would be an error of estimand: one is an unpaired between-arm contrast, the other a within-case paired contrast. The second is the paired contrast that does carry a range.

R1-8.title: Memory promotion can propagate stable VLM errors
R1-8.asks: frequency >= 3 and consistency >= 0.80 and >= 1 VLM resolution does not guarantee semantic correctness; handle negation; escalate on conflict.

metrics.promotion_rule: frequency >= 3 AND consistency >= 0.8 AND >= 1 L3b resolution

R1-9.title: Visual confirmation, with the controlled presence/absence arm first
R1-9.asks: Relate confirmation outcomes to the memory statistics that drove them.

primary_controlled_experiment.design: the same instruction, the same code and ontology, on both platforms, with the referent object present in one arm and physically removed in the other
primary_controlled_experiment.claim: 8/8 controlled presence/absence trials were classified consistently with the physical scene. The non-confirmations in the absent arm are correct outputs, not confirmation failures.

descriptive_positive_confirmation_preval.definition: share of positive confirmations among attempted checks. This is a prevalence, not an accuracy: it has no ground truth behind it and it counts the correct refusals of the absent arm as negatives. Do not label it confirmation accuracy.

metrics.observability_note: Confirmation is attempted only where a POI signature exists. Nodes without one are never confirmed and never counted as failures; that asymmetry is reported rather than absorbed into a rate.

R1-10.title: Frozen-implementation validation campaign
R1-10.asks: A complete re-run against a frozen, identified implementation.

metrics.framing: Session E is not a repetition of sessions A-C. It is a new, reviewer-driven campaign run entirely against a frozen implementation that every record identifies cryptographically. v4.8-review contains the corrections made in response to review, so calling it a re-run of the earlier campaign would misdescribe it.
metrics.note: Every run records the full commit hash and git_dirty. The code revision that produced any record is therefore fixed cryptographically, and can be verified against any source later provided, without the source being published now.

metrics.mechanism: one platform resolves by L3b; the extractor compiles the repeated result into the shared digest; the other platform then serves it at cascade step 0 without a VLM call
metrics.what_it_is_not: paraphrase generalization. The negative control in the same block uses a semantically similar instruction with no lexical overlap against the stored association; it does not match M3 and escalates. What transfers is a learned lexical instruction-node association.

R2-6.title: Concurrent VLM inference on a shared server
R2-6.asks: Insufficient testing of concurrent VLM inference.

metrics.interpretation: Concurrent two-robot operation stayed functionally correct, but simultaneous access to the single shared inference server produced a large and asymmetric end-to-end latency spread, and which platform was the slower one changed between pairs. That identifies the shared server as a fleet-scaling bottleneck.
metrics.what_the_data_does_not_support: It does not establish that the server serialises requests. The recorded queue_ms is of the order of one millisecond and cannot account for a spread of several seconds, so the timing was not decomposed at the server. The observation is consistent with contention or partial serialisation; the instrumentation cannot separate them.

R2-9.title: Semantic reasoning vs physical execution, at run level
R2-9.asks: Analyse the navigation failure rate; separate L3 reasoning errors from L1 execution; quantify the heterogeneous-hardware effect.

terminal_failures_raw.definition: every run in the archive whose last record is a miss

detail.invalidation_reason: externally invalidated during the session (localization collapse from an external cause) and re-run under the protocol; the completed re-run is the observation of record

terminal_failures_protocol_valid.definition: runs the protocol did not invalidate. This is the figure for the primary analysis; the raw count above is kept so the archive and the analysis reconcile.

excluded.reason: externally invalidated during the session (localization collapse from an external cause) and re-run under the protocol; the completed re-run is the observation of record

metrics.counting_note: 18 decision records carry nav_outcome = missed, but only 2 runs end in one. The rest are recovery cycles inside runs that subsequently completed. The two numbers must never be interchanged.

per_platform.basis: protocol-valid runs (the invalidated run is excluded)

per_platform_raw_for_reconciliation.basis: every archived run, including the protocol-invalidated one. Kept so the archive and the analysis reconcile; not part of the primary inferential analysis.

platform_terminal_miss_fisher.basis: protocol-valid runs only; the invalidated run is excluded
platform_terminal_miss_fisher.note: Reported for completeness. With this many terminal failures the comparison has almost no power and must not be presented as evidence of a platform difference.

semantic_vs_execution.note: Every terminal failure listed above reached a decision; none is a failure to resolve the instruction. Resolution and execution are therefore separable in this dataset.

metrics.status: PENDING — requires a replay of the recorded prompts through a second model
metrics.note: Every escalated record stores extra.vlm_prompt_full, the complete prompt as sent. Together with the model digest this makes the comparison reproducible by a third party without any of our code. The second-model run itself is not yet done and this key must not be cited until it is.
